2 · Model Assumptions

  • Quasi-static longitudinal model; no rotational inertia of rotor or driveline.
  • Gearbox efficiency applied directionally: torque divided by η when motoring, multiplied when regenerating.
  • Battery power built from wheel power, so the gearbox loss is counted exactly once.
  • Motor efficiency from the supplied map; the negative-torque half is mirrored from the positive half (assumption, not measurement).
  • Shifting is instantaneous and lossless — no torque interruption, synchronisation or inertia cost.
  • No auxiliary load, no pack I²R loss, no separate inverter model.
  • Objective is consumed motor input energy, ∫max(Pbatt, 0) dt, with regeneration excluded.

Data provenance

These numbers come from reconstructed stand-in data, not the real N603 log. The original CSV and XLSX were unavailable, so both inputs were rebuilt by fitting to every diagnostic the notebook printed. Sample count, duration, peak speed, map shape, invalid-cell count, peak efficiency and its location, and the 44 baseline upshifts all match exactly; energy and fallback counts match within a few percent. The conclusions reproduce, but do not quote these figures as N603 results.

Why this result is not usable

The reported optimum is 22.0 / 22.0 km/h — upshift equal to downshift. That is a zero-width hysteresis band, not a gear strategy: the controller upshifts and downshifts on consecutive samples, 366 times over the cycle, against 44 for the baseline.

Immediately below that result the notebook prints "Optimization validation passed: every combined candidate has downshift speed below upshift speed." That assertion guards only the combined grid; the upshift-only case is never checked. The manual-verification cell also passes on this strategy, because it asserts only internal energy consistency (consumed − recovered = net), never whether the strategy is physically possible.

Every one of the three optimisation cases lands on an edge of its own search range. An optimiser that returns the corner of its box has not found an optimum.

Vehicle longitudinal dynamics

Speed, wheel torque and wheel power from the road-load decomposition (inertia + rolling + aerodynamic + grade).

Reading this figure

Wheel torque looks like a hairball because acceleration comes from np.gradient of an unfiltered 1 Hz log. That noise is roughly zero-mean in power, but the objective integrates max(P, 0), which rectifies it and adds energy that was never demanded.

Reading this figure

Peak 94.13 % at 4 260 rpm / 13.0 Nm. The blank upper-right region is the 14 672 missing cells — they correspond almost exactly to the area above the constant-power curve, which is why the nearest-neighbour fallback ends up filling infeasible points.

Actual gear-transition movement

Where each shift moves the operating point, with vehicle speed labelled.

Reading this figure

Upshifts drop motor speed by the ratio gap (19 -> 11) and raise torque — moving the point toward the high-efficiency island. This is the real mechanism behind the trend.

Consumed motor input energy vs upshift speed

The optimisation curve. Red marker = reported minimum.

Reading this figure

The marker sits at 22 km/h — equal to the downshift threshold, i.e. a zero-width hysteresis band. The curve rises monotonically from there to the top of the range. This is an optimum pinned to the boundary of its own search box, and nothing on the chart signals that.

Three-case threshold optimisation

Upshift-only, downshift-only, and the combined grid.

Reading this figure

All three land on a range edge: upshift 22 (floor region), downshift 5 (floor of 5-31), combined (22, 11). The heatmap shades continuously darker toward the bottom-left corner — the optimiser is being pulled out of the searched box. Selected optimum strategy

Speed, gear state, motor RPM and battery power for the reported best strategy.

Reading this figure

The gear-state panel is a solid block: this strategy shifts 366 times. No AMT can do that, and the model charges nothing for it.

What the study should conclude

Cruise sits at 3–7 Nm on a 45 Nm motor (6–15 % load) in both ratios. Peak map efficiency is 13.0 Nm × 4 260 rpm = 5.80 kW of shaft power, while the cycle's mean battery power is 8.73 kWh / 7.88 h = 1.10 kW — 19 % of that.

A gear ratio moves the operating point along an iso-power hyperbola, trading torque against speed. It cannot move the point between hyperbolas. So no shift schedule and no ratio choice reaches the high-efficiency island: the demand is a 1–2 kW point and the island is a 5.8 kW point.

The motor is oversized for this duty by roughly a factor of five. That is the finding this study should report — not an 85–113 Wh shift-threshold saving that sits inside the model's own error bar.
